content.title: A useful ladder
content.text:
For the simple cases in this lesson, think in this order:

1. Does the rule match the element? 2. Is one rule more specifically targeted? 3. If the relevant rules are otherwise equal, which one comes later?

feedback.correct: The class-targeted rules outrank the type rule here, and the later class rule wins between the two class rules.
feedback.incorrect: The class-targeted rules outrank the type rule here, and the later class rule wins between the two class rules.

options.text: Change the first color and leave the conflicting rule in place.
Remove or change the conflicting later rule so the intended rule is the one that remains.

feedback.correct: A good fix removes the unnecessary conflict instead of stacking more rules on top.
feedback.incorrect: A good fix removes the unnecessary conflict instead of stacking more rules on top.

options.text: The last rule always wins no matter what.
Only one CSS rule can match an element.
The cascade resolves conflicts among matching rules using their relative priority and order.

feedback.correct: The cascade is a conflict-resolution system. “Last wins” is only a safe shortcut when the relevant priority conditions are equal.
feedback.incorrect: The cascade is a conflict-resolution system. “Last wins” is only a safe shortcut when the relevant priority conditions are equal.
